newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Feb 27.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Feb 27.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Thursday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
BUSINESS DAY

- The so-called HIV protease inhibitor Virodene was nothing more than an industrial solvent and no scientific evidence existed that it would act against the virus, the committee appointed to investigate the alleged discovery of an AIDS drug found.

- The cost of mailing a standard letter could rise by as much as fourty percent to one rand next week if the Post Office's proposals to boost revenue and counter future reductions in the state subsidy are accepted by government, Post Office managing director Frank Touwen said on Wednesday.
- South African Students Congress members intensified their campaign on Wednesday to force government to abandon plans to slash subsidies.

- Taxpayers have paid the 18 members of the Volkstaat Council more than four million rands in salaries and allowances to pursue the idea of an independent homeland for Afrikaners somewhere in South Africa.
BUSINESS REPORT
- Mutual & Federal is poised to take up 20,000 square metres in the Old Mutual Centre tower block in the largest lease deal seen in the Johannesburg central business district in nine years.

- Intense competition in the motor industry had a negative effect on Toyota South Africa in the year to December 31, resulting in operating income slumping 8.1 percent to 308.39 million rand from 335.75 million rand for the corresponding period in the previous year, the company said.

- The Standing Advisory Comittee on Company Law has recommended that holdings in listed companies through nominees should be disclosed once they reach ten percent, a source close to the committee said on Wednesday.
SAKE BEELD
- An increase in the cost of mailing is expected by Tuesday, Post Office director of South Africa, Frank Touwen said on Wednesday.

- A massive property development, which will eventually be equivalent to fourty percent of Johannesburg's central business district, will emerge in the south western area of the city over the next ten years.
- Visa International is going to issue a new smart in South Africa which will give bank clients credit convenience, debit convenience, a electronic exchange and prearranged overdrafts on one card.
THE STAR

- The researchers who developed Virodene PO58, hailed as an Aids wonder drug, were rapped on the knuckles on Wednesday for contravening accepted scientific procedures and conducting trials on patients without sufficient evidence.

- Three policemen were injured, one of them seriously, when they were attacked by stone-throwing students at the University of the North, near Pietersburg in the Northern Province, late on Wednesday afternoon.
- Damage estimated at least 100,000 rand was caused on Wednesday when an oversized truck struck the support-work for a new bridge being built over the Ben Schoeman Highway near Midrand.
- An eight-year-old boy suffering from Aids is to be admitted to Melpark Primary School in Melville from next term following an agreement between the boy's foster mother and the school on Wednesday.
